intentions.title: Give the Next.js demo one server-only, authenticated, tenancy-scoped path into the Barkpark API so no upstream token or fetch ever leaks to the browser
intentions.evidence: barkpark-client.ts (`import "server-only"`, BARKPARK_TOKEN never NEXT_PUBLIC_, per-request createClient scoping to /w/:workspace/p/:project vs flat /v1/... back-compat) and bp-fetch.ts (authHeaders/withAuth centralising the bearer, `server-only` guard) are the single choke point every reader/finder/search module goes through.

intentions.title: Keep every upstream call resilient across a Phoenix deploy/restart window without ever surfacing a raw JSON.parse crash or a stuck serverless slot
intentions.evidence: bp-fetch.ts: AbortController timeout (15s default), 2 retries with 1s/2s backoff over TRANSIENT_STATUS {502,503,504}, res.ok guard before body consumption, defensive text()->JSON.parse, BpUpstreamError distinguishing `definitive` (real {error:...} envelope, never retried) vs transient/network (status 0) failures, humanUpstreamMessage translating restarts into a friendly message.

intentions.title: Drive precise, targeted cache invalidation from Studio publish events instead of blunt full-site revalidation
intentions.evidence: bp-tags.ts implements the bp:ds:<dataset>:{_all,doc:<id>,type:<type>} tag scheme mirroring docs/contracts/webhook-realtime.md so Phoenix Webhooks.Dispatcher -> /api/barkpark/webhook -> revalidateTag() busts exactly the affected reader/finder caches; posts.ts/get-post.ts consume bpAll/bpType via unstable_cache.

intentions.title: Offer two complementary search engines (exact/operator-aware Postgres, typo-tolerant Indx) behind one always-fresh, never-cached search contract with anti-gaming session attribution
intentions.evidence: find-search.ts's runSearch: no-store on every call, engine selection with token-gated scoped route for Indx vs anonymous flat route, X-BP-SEARCH-CLIENT/X-BP-SEARCH-RECORD headers for query-event recording tied to a browser session id, CONTENT_TYPES_CSV allowlist so private config schemas never leak into browse/facets; find.ts defines the shared FindHit/ParsedQuery/FacetMap contract and the unified /d/[type]/[slug] reader routing (readerHref) so no doc type is a dead end.

intentions.title: Faithfully reconstruct every generated Barkpark content type (posts, papers, sheets) client-side from the same production schema the API emits, without hand-maintained types drifting from it
intentions.evidence: papers.ts/posts.ts derive PaperDocument/PostDocument as generated Paper/Post & BarkparkDocument plus documented demo-only deltas (explicit comments citing deletion of old hand-written duplicate types); sheets.ts documents the sparse-to-dense grid model (densifyTab, MERGE_AREA_CAP=10_000 kept in lockstep with api/lib/.../walk.ex's @merge_area_cap) so the same hostile-doc guard exists on both server and browser.

intentions.title: Enforce structural (not pixel) parity of composed PortableDoc component blocks across Elixir, web, and Go/TUI renderers via a shared golden-projection contract
intentions.evidence: component-projections.ts maps each authored component block to the same element-tree projection the Elixir generator emits into <type>.golden.json, asserted equal by __tests__/component-golden-parity.test.ts; STATUS_LADDER hard-mirrors design/status-manifest.json; comments explicitly log SUBSET-PARITY exceptions (pipeline, roadmap) as filed, not papered over.

intentions.title: Prevent CMS-authored content from executing script or navigating off-site via unsafe link schemes in the rendered reader
intentions.evidence: safe-href.ts's safeHref allow-lists http/https/mailto/tel plus a narrow set of relative forms, explicitly rejecting javascript:/data: and protocol-relative //host (and its backslash-normalized form), documented as parity with the Elixir safe_url and Go sanitizeURL sibling implementations.
